pytorch.reason: parametrize SO(3) circle R(theta)=exp(theta*L3); compute ||R(2*pi)-I||~0 (period); winding proxy via angle tracking

pyg.reason: not used — torus winding is matrix-parametric; no graph message-passing required

z3.reason: UNSAT: winding number = 0 AND path is non-contractible (non-contractible torus path must have nonzero winding)

cvc5.reason: not used — z3 covers the proof layer for this sim

sympy.reason: symbolic: eigenvalues of R(theta)=exp(theta*L3) are e^{+-i*theta},1; period 2pi; SU(3) torus det=1 symbolic verification

clifford.reason: Clifford torus in Cl(4,0): R1=cos(t1)+sin(t1)*e12, R2=cos(t2)+sin(t2)*e34; they commute; independent product IS the T^2 torus

geomstats.reason: not used — torus winding is handled by sympy/clifford/torch; no manifold sampling needed for this test

e3nn.reason: not used — torus winding is matrix algebraic; no equivariant network required

rustworkx.reason: torus winding graph: nodes labeled by (w1,w2) torus position; edges=single winding step; verify graph is periodic

xgi.reason: hyperedge {T1_circle, T2_torus, Axis5} connecting the SO(3) circle and SU(3) torus to Axis 5 — topology of the torus bundle

toponetx.reason: not used — torus structure is handled by xgi hyperedges; no cell complex required

gudhi.reason: not used — torus winding is algebraic; no persistent homology required

P1_pytorch_so3_circle_period_2pi.description: T^1 in SO(3): R(2*pi) = I exactly — circle has period 2*pi (one full winding)

P2_pytorch_so3_circle_constant_norm.description: R(theta) has constant Frobenius norm = sqrt(3) for all theta — uniform circle

P3_pytorch_su3_torus_det1.description: SU(3) maximal torus T^2: det(diag(e^it1, e^it2, e^{-i(t1+t2)})) = 1 for all (t1,t2)

P4_pytorch_so3_angle_one_full_winding.description: R(theta)[0,0] = cos(theta) crosses zero exactly 2 times in [0,2pi] — one full winding

P5_sympy_so3_circle_eigenvalues.description: Sympy: R(theta)=exp(theta*L3) has eigenvalue 1 (fixed axis) plus complex pair e^{+-i*theta}

P6_sympy_su3_torus_det1_symbolic.description: Sympy: det(diag(e^it1, e^it2, e^{-i(t1+t2)})) = 1 symbolically verified

P7_clifford_torus_rotors_commute.description: Clifford torus: R1=cos(t1)+sin(t1)*e12 and R2=cos(t2)+sin(t2)*e34 commute ([R1,R2]=0)

P8_clifford_torus_product_traces_T2.description: Clifford torus: R1(t1=0)*R2 = R2 exactly; product traces T^2 as (t1,t2) vary independently

P9_rustworkx_torus_winding_graph_periodi.description: Torus winding graph: 4 nodes for (w1,w2) in {0,1}^2; 4 edges for w1-stepping — periodic Z structure

N1_pytorch_half_winding_not_closed.description: Negative: R(pi) != I — path of half-winding does not close; winding number = 1/2 is not an integer

N2_z3_noncontractible_path_nonzero_windi.description: Z3 UNSAT: winding=0 AND path is non-contractible — non-contractible loop must have nonzero winding

N3_sympy_so3_circle_basepoint_identity.description: Sympy: R(theta=0) = I (base point of the circle T^1 in SO(3)); winding = 0 at base

N4_clifford_same_rotor_trivially_commute.description: Negative control: R1*R1 - R1*R1 = 0 trivially; T^2 requires TWO independent e12 and e34 planes

N5_rustworkx_base_winding_no_incoming.description: Negative: base point (winding=0) has no incoming edges — it is the start of the winding sequence

B1_pytorch_theta_2pi_full_winding.description: Boundary: theta=2*pi completes exactly one winding; R(2*pi)=I within numerical precision

B2_sympy_su3_torus_basepoint_identity.description: Sympy boundary: SU(3) torus at (t1=0, t2=0) = I — base point of T^2 has winding (0,0)

B3_pytorch_winding0_vs_1_both_close.description: Boundary: both winding=0 (constant) and winding=1 (full circle) paths close at base point; topology distinguishes them

B4_clifford_torus_basepoint_is_scalar1.description: Clifford torus at (t1=0, t2=0): R1*R2 = 1 (scalar) — base point winding=(0,0)

B5_z3_winding1_noncontractible_sat.description: Z3 SAT: winding=1 AND non-contractible is consistent — the T^1 circle has exactly this property

B6_xgi_torus_axis5_hyperedge.description: XGI hyperedge {T1_circle, T2_torus, Axis5} connects the SO(3) circle and SU(3) torus to Axis 5

B7_rustworkx_period4_ring_has_path.description: Boundary: 4-node ring graph has a path from node 0 to node 3 — the winding sequence is periodic
